config.title: Write exhaustive switch using never

intro.title: Write exhaustive switch using never
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple TypeScript function that uses a switch statement to handle different cases of a union type. You will learn the core concept of using the 'never' type to create an exhaustive switch, which ensures your code handles all possible cases and prevents runtime errors. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type system, union types, and the 'never' type. This approach helps catch missing cases at compile time, making your code more robust and maintainable. By the end, you'll understand how to write safer, exhaustive conditionals in TypeScript.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building robust, type-safe state machines in real-world UI components. For example, in a complex dashboard with multiple data visualization modes (chart, table, map, summary), each mode can be a distinct union type. An exhaustive switch ensures every possible view state is handled, preventing runtime errors when a new mode is added. Similarly, in a multi-step form or a checkout flow, it guarantees all user progression states (cart, shipping, payment, confirmation) have defined UI logic, making the application more maintainable and predictable.

objectives: Implement a basic switch statement that handles all possible cases for a union type.
Apply the `never` type to represent code that should never be executed.
Construct an exhaustive switch by adding a default case that assigns the remaining value to a variable of type `never`.
Configure TypeScript to produce a compile-time error when a new case is added to the union but not handled in the switch.
Manipulate a union type by adding new members and observing the resulting type errors.
Initialize a variable with a union type and use it in an exhaustive switch statement.
Integrate an exhaustive switch pattern into a function that returns different values based on the input type.

steps.title: Import TypeScript and define a discriminated union type
steps.instruction: Create a discriminated union type called Shape with circle, square, and triangle variants using literal type properties.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword with union syntax (|) and include a literal property like 'kind' or 'type' to distinguish each variant.

steps.title: Add a new member to the Shape union
steps.instruction: Add a new 'rectangle' variant to the Shape union type. This variant should have 'kind' set to 'rectangle' and include 'width' and 'height' properties, both of type number.
steps.hint: Remember that a discriminated union type is defined using the 'type' keyword with the '|' operator. Add 'rectangle' as another option in the union, following the same pattern as the existing variants.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a new variant to a union type
type Vehicle = { type: 'car'; wheels: number } | { type: 'bike'; pedals: number } | { type: 'boat'; sails: number };
steps.expectedOutcome: The Shape union type now includes a rectangle variant, making it a union of four distinct shapes.
successCriteria: The Shape type is updated to include a rectangle variant with the correct properties: kind: 'rectangle', width: number, and height: number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a rectangle variant, but check that it has the correct properties: kind should be 'rectangle', and both width and height should be numbers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Shape union type was not updated correctly. Ensure you add a rectangle variant with the required properties to the existing union.

steps.instruction: Look at the getArea function and notice that TypeScript is showing an error because the switch statement doesn't handle all possible Shape union members.
steps.hint: Check the TypeScript error message - it should indicate that not all code paths return a value, which means the switch statement is incomplete.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should see a TypeScript error indicating that the function lacks a return statement for all code paths, specifically that the switch statement doesn't handle all Shape variants.
successCriteria: TypeScript shows an error in the getArea function because the switch statement doesn't cover all possible Shape union members.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Look for the TypeScript error message in your editor - it should indicate that not all code paths return a value in the getArea function.

steps.title: Add a default case with never type assertion
steps.instruction: Add a default case to the switch statement that assigns the shape parameter to a variable of type never and throws an error.
steps.hint: After your existing case blocks, add 'default:' followed by a variable assignment like 'const _exhaustiveCheck: never = shape;' then throw an error.
steps.expectedOutcome: The switch statement now has a default case that uses the never type for exhaustive checking.
successCriteria: The default case includes a variable assignment of shape to type never and throws an error.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a default case, but it's missing either the never type assertion or the error throw. Make sure to assign shape to a variable of type never and throw an error.
